newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends rangebound session weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends rangebound session weaker.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back modestly in subdued trade on Friday, pressured by light speculative and local selling, traders said.
Prices spent the bulk of the session in negative territory, but steady scale-down trade buying trimmed losses, confining prices to a tight range and preventing a test of key chart support.
"It was a range day, a nothing day," one trader said. "It (the March contract) ran out of steam above 116.00 and below 115.50."

Key March delivery fell to a session low of 115.30 cents a lb, just shy of the widely watched 115.00-cent support level. By the close, March stood at 116.25 cents, down 0.40 cent a lb on the day, to 116.65 cents. March reached a high of 116.75.
Second-position May ended 0.60 cent lower, at 114.35, while the rest finished 0.25 to 1.25 weaker.

With little fresh fundamental input, traders said the market continued to trade technically. They said after the 115.00-cent mark, the March contract's next downside target was seen at 112.00 cents, then 110.00 cents. Resistance was pegged at 117.50 cents, followed by 119.00-120.00 cents.
Traders await the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders Report, anticipating the figures will show a substantial increase in non-commercial long positions.

The biweekly report for the weeks ended December 24 and December 31 will be issued on Monday, January 6, after 1530 EST (2030 GMT) -- a one day delay due to this week's New Year's holiday, the CFTC said..
The day's volume thin, at an estimated at 5,300 lots, traders said.
